title: Towards synergy between theory and experiments: First-passage processes under resetting with stochastic return protocols
abstract: Stochastic resetting with stochastic return (SR) has recently emerged as an effective and practically relevant strategy for controlling first-passage phenomena and optimizing search processes by significantly reducing completion times in a wide class of stochastic systems. While most theoretical studies assume instantaneous return (IR), in realistic systems the return to the resetting position typically occurs over a finite time. We consider a 1-d diffusing particle in a harmonic trap with stiffnesses $k_1$ and $k_2$ during search and return, respectively. The particle searches for the target and, upon resetting at rate $r$, enters the return phase, continuing until it reaches either the origin or the absorbing target at $L>0$. Notably, the model permits target detection throughout the return phase, distinguishing it from IR scenarios. We analytically derive the MFPT for our model and determine parameter regions where SR enhances or suppresses search efficiency over the underlying dynamics, constructing the corresponding phase diagram using the coefficient of variation criterion. We further identify regimes in which SR is more efficient than IR using the SR criterion. This behavior is tested across different parameter sets taken from experimental studies by Goerlich et al., Biroli et al., and Besga et al. We map the parameter values reported in existing experimental studies onto our theoretical phase diagram, thereby identifying the regimes in which SR outperforms IR. In particular, we find that the most relevant region of the phase space, where SR is most beneficial corresponds to larger values of the potential strength in the search phase and lower values of potential in the return phase. Our results provide experimentally testable predictions and bridge the gap between theoretical resetting models and optical trap mediated finite-time return dynamics.
summary: This paper analyzes search processes using Stochastic Resetting with Stochastic Return (SR) in a 1D harmonic trap model. By deriving the Mean First-Passage Time and using efficiency criteria, the authors map out the parameter space where SR significantly improves search speed compared to instantaneous return. The findings offer crucial, experimentally verifiable guidelines for optimizing search protocols in physical systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates first-passage processes under Stochastic Resetting with Stochastic Return (SR) protocols to determine how this mechanism controls search efficiency compared to standard Instantaneous Return (IR) models.
main_result: The most beneficial regime for SR is found to occur when the potential strength in the search phase ($k_1$) is large and the potential strength in the return phase ($k_2$) is small.
method: The authors analytically derive the Mean First-Passage Time (MFPT) and utilize the coefficient-of-variation (CV) criterion and a stochastic return criterion to construct phase diagrams comparing SR and IR performance.
model_or_system: The model considers a one-dimensional diffusing particle undergoing an overdamped Langevin process confined in a harmonic trap. The process involves a search phase (stiffness $k_1$) followed by a stochastic return phase (stiffness $k_2$) after resetting at rate $r$.
key_observables: Mean First-Passage Time (MFPT), search efficiency enhancement/suppression (via CV criterion), and the comparison of SR vs. IR performance.
important_parameters: Trap stiffnesses ($k_1, k_2$), resetting rate ($r$), and target location ($L$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) process in both phases, and the analysis explicitly accounts for target detection during the finite-time return phase.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the search process under different scenarios (direct success, target hit during return, or return to origin) and present phase diagrams mapping SR benefit based on parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general framework of SR protocols, derives the MFPT analytically, and then applies diagnostic criteria (CV, SR criterion) to map out the parameter space where the stochastic return mechanism provides a measurable advantage over instantaneous return.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical framework for optimizing search processes in physical systems, offering experimentally testable predictions that bridge abstract theoretical models of resetting with concrete dynamics found in optical trap experiments.
